The nominal chemical composition of the MAR-M247 superalloy is 10% Co, 10% W, 8.4% Cr, 5.5% Al, 3% Ta, 1.4% Hf, 1.1% Ti, 0.65% Mo, 0.05% Zr, 0.015% B, and 0.15% C.

Thermodynamic simulations using the Scheil model predicted the solidification sequence, including the formation of the γ phase at 1397°C, followed by the precipitation of MC carbides and Ni(Hf,Zr) intermetallic phases.
X-ray diffraction analysis identified the presence of the γ matrix, γ' precipitates, MC carbides, M5B3 borides, and Ni(Hf,Zr) intermetallic phases in the as-cast MAR-M247 superalloy.
The ultimate tensile strength of the produced castings ranged from 970 MPa to 1088 MPa, depending on the casting parameters.

The volume fraction of secondary γ' precipitates in the dendritic regions decreased from 51% to 50% when the withdrawal rate was increased from 3.4 mm/min to 5.0 mm/min for the 1510°C mold preheating temperature.

The partitioning coefficient (k) for W was greater than 1, indicating its enrichment in the dendritic regions, while elements like Cr, Ti, Ta, and Hf had k<1, meaning they segregated to the interdendritic regions.
